recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future invariant changes should continue to add focused invariant-tests fixtures with the resource/profile change; broader contributor-process documentation, if desired, should be handled separately rather than as a FHIR-24664 conformance source fix.
issue_request: FHIR-24664 was a Published FHIR-I change request, resolved Persuasive, asking that newly introduced resource constraints have at least a couple of unit tests asserting that the actual FHIRPath expression works. The Jira description linked the CareTeam ctm-1 validation discussion as input.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-24664 was found. The application trail is visible in the 2023-02-16 committers Zulip discussion describing source/*/invariant-tests fail fixtures that stop the build, and in subsequent source commits such as 116d8de8f17ae3a3bda6704ca1122fb03eb131de, which added CareTeam ctm-1 and ctm-2 invariant failure tests.
additional_context: FHIR-24860, already represented on the combined branch by 46d1774d28765c39bbbcb0014445e47510081c58, supports the same QA direction: explicitly check invariants during review rather than infer them automatically. FHIR-42928 later removed the original CareTeam ctm-1 onBehalfOf/Practitioner invariant and broadened CareTeam.participant.onBehalfOf, so the old motivating constraint is no longer active current source.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source edit is needed because invariant-test fixtures are already in active use across the source tree, CareTeam is in build scope, and current CareTeam source has only active ctm-2 with a matching failure fixture.
